content: Fernline Studio does one open garden day a year for the Whitlow family garden, usually in June, for the local community.
Tomasz keeps a spare set of site tools in the van at all times, saves a trip back to the studio.
The studio's public liability insurance renews in October, Dana handles the renewal paperwork.
Priya is working part of her week on a personal portfolio project, unrelated to studio clients.
Little Acorns nursery closes for two weeks over the summer, usually the last week of July and first week of August.
The task app has a tag system, studio tasks and personal tasks are kept in separate tags.
Dana Okafor also does books for two other small local businesses, not exclusive to Fernline Studio.
The Halden Parks Trust meadow project is the first big public project the studio has taken on.
Sam is training for a half marathon in the autumn, runs most weekday mornings before work.
The studio's design software licence renews annually every February, gets paid from the business account.
Rui is starting to recognise a few plant names, favourite is the sunflower.
Fernline Studio does not do lawn mowing or ongoing garden maintenance, only design and planting projects.
The bank app lets Dana view transactions but not move money, read only access set up in March.
Sam picks Rui up from Little Acorns nursery on Mondays and Wednesdays, Jordan does the rest of the week's pickups.
Oakridge Housing Co-op's 2026 courtyard summer fair happened on 2026-07-18, Fernline Studio had a planting demo stand again like last year.
Priya is Fernline Studio's designer, she draws up planting plans and most of the client presentation boards.
Fernline Studio is Jordan's practice, three people: Jordan, Priya, and Tomasz, based on Mill Lane in Marrowbrook.

First proper week back after the new year. Priya is finishing up the planting boards for a small residential enquiry near Oakridge village, still not confirmed as a project yet, just a paid quote stage. Tomasz spent two days at the Whitlow family garden clearing the old shrubs from the side bed ready for the spring planting plan, slower going than expected because of the frozen ground. The studio van needed a new wiper blade, sorted that at the garage on Mill Lane along with the usual service check. Jordan spent most of Thursday and Friday on the Halden Parks Trust meadow drawings, the first full draft is nearly ready to send over for their board to look at. Also spent some time updating the studio's supplier list since a couple of the old contacts have left their companies and the emails were bouncing. Nothing major to flag for next week, just the usual mix of drawing time and a site visit booked for Wednesday morning at Oakridge.

Quiet weekend at home. Rui had a cold most of the week so stayed off nursery on the Thursday and Friday, back to normal by Saturday. Sam did a big food shop and sorted the loft a bit, found a box of old garden magazines that got passed on to the studio instead of the bin since Priya wanted to look through them. Pickle had his nails clipped at the groomers on Mill Lane, he hates it every time but it only takes ten minutes. Jordan spent Sunday morning doing paperwork at the kitchen table while Sam took Rui and Pickle to the park. Talked about maybe getting the kitchen tap fixed, it has been dripping for a couple of weeks, added it to the task app under home jobs. Also spent a bit of time going through old photos to put together a small album for Sam's parents, something to do on a rainy Sunday afternoon rather than sit in front of the television. The recycling bin was overflowing again after the weekend shop, worth remembering that collection day moved to Tuesday this year rather than Wednesday like it used to be before the council changed the schedule. Nothing else major, just an ordinary weekend before a busier week with two site visits booked.

Notes from going through the accounts with Dana this month. Income for February was a bit lower than January because of the slow start after the holidays, nothing to worry about, March already looks busier with the Oakridge and Halden invoices going out. Dana suggested setting up a separate small pot for equipment replacement since the studio printer is getting old and will need replacing this year or next. Also discussed whether to take on a fourth person at some point, decided it is too early to think about seriously until the Halden project and the college course workload settle into a rhythm. The business savings account earned a small amount of interest, barely worth mentioning but Dana likes to note it anyway for the annual return. Reminder to self, keep receipts for the new site survey pads and the tape measures, small purchases add up and Dana likes them itemised rather than lumped together.

First class of the spring term went well, good turnout, thirteen people signed up which is more than last term. Went through the basics of site analysis in week one, planning to cover soil types and drainage in week two. One student mentioned they used to work in horticulture years ago and asked some sharper questions than most, good for keeping the pace up. The college's projector in the usual room is a bit dim, put in a request with the college admin office to get it looked at before it becomes a problem for showing planting photos properly. Also need to remember to bring printed handouts each week since not everyone likes reading off a screen, the college print room takes a day to turn around requests so plan ahead. A couple of students introduced themselves as neighbours who just wanted to make their own gardens nicer rather than anyone with a professional interest, which is a nice mix for the group discussions. Looking forward to the first site walk in week four, weather permitting, it usually goes down well with the group.

Spent an afternoon tidying up the digital side of things. Went through the notes app and archived a bunch of old project folders from finished jobs, kept the current ones easier to find. The task app had a handful of duplicate recurring tasks from a glitch a while back, deleted the extras. Checked the calendar app is still showing all three calendars correctly on the phone after the last update, seems fine. Also updated the passwords for a couple of the supplier logins since it had been a long while and the password manager flagged them as old. Went through the personal mailbox too and set up a couple of filters to keep newsletters out of the main inbox, should cut down on the daily clutter a bit going forward. Thought about whether the studio needs a proper backup routine for the notes app content beyond what the app itself keeps, decided to look into it another day since nothing has ever actually been lost so far. Nothing broke, just routine upkeep that tends to get put off for months at a time until an afternoon opens up for it.

Site visit round up. Went to the Whitlow family garden in the morning, the new planting along the back border is establishing well, a couple of the roses need replacing since they did not survive the transplant, Thornfield have them in stock for next week. Afternoon was spent at Halden Parks Trust walking the meadow area with Marcus, he is happy with progress and mentioned the trust's board would like a short presentation at their June meeting, need to prepare some slides for that. Oakridge Housing Co-op's irrigation contractor called to say the trenching for the last section will start a week later than planned because of a delay getting a part, not a big issue since the planting for that section was not due to start until after anyway. Stopped by the stationer on the way back to the studio to pick up more survey pads since the box in the van was nearly empty again. Overall a good week, just a lot of driving between the three sites and not much time left for drawing, will need to catch up on that over the weekend instead.

Rui finished the first block of swimming lessons, moved up a group, quite pleased about it. Sam's parents visited for the weekend as planned, went well, Rui loved having them around and Pickle got extra walks out of it. The hedge finally got trimmed, hired someone rather than doing it at the weekend like usual, worth every penny given how long it always takes doing it alone. Also sorted through Rui's old clothes that no longer fit, bagged up for a charity shop drop off next week. Jordan and Sam talked about maybe a short holiday in the autumn once the college course finishes for term, nothing booked yet just an idea floated over dinner. Rui asked a lot of questions about where Sam's parents live and whether Pickle could come too on any future trip, which will need thinking about depending on where they end up going. The greenhouse seedlings are coming along nicely, a few will be ready to go into client projects by midsummer if they keep growing at this rate.

Invoicing catch up for the half year. Most clients are paying on time, Oakridge Housing Co-op is usually the slowest but never more than a week or two late, their finance approvals go through the board which is just how they work. Sent the Whitlow family their latest invoice for the planting phase, they always pay within a couple of days which is appreciated. Dana mentioned the studio might be close to needing quarterly VAT payments on account rather than annual, will keep an eye on it over the next couple of quarters before deciding anything. Also looked at whether the invoicing tool's reporting could break down income by client automatically, turns out it can with a filter, useful for next time doing the year end summary. Spent a bit of time double checking the half year totals against the bank statement, everything matched up which is always a relief given how many small supplier payments go through in a typical month. Dana said the half year position is the healthiest it has been since the studio started, mostly down to the Halden and Oakridge contracts landing when they did.

Notes before the autumn term starts next week. Eleven people signed up so far, a bit lower than spring but still a decent group, enrolment sometimes trickles in during the first couple of weeks anyway. Printed the welcome pack at the college print room, includes the course outline and a reading list, mostly general planting design books available at the Marrowbrook library. Emailed the college admin office to confirm the room booking one more time since the room changed earlier in the summer, want to be sure everything lines up before the first class. Also thinking about adding a short section on maintenance this term based on feedback from spring, a few students said they wanted more of that even though it is not strictly the course focus. Went through last term's feedback forms properly this time rather than skimming them, a few useful suggestions about pacing the middle weeks better since that is when attendance usually dips a little. Looking forward to getting back into a rhythm with the college course now the summer break is over.

Supplier round up for the quarter. Thornfield Growers have been solid since the studio switched over, good stock availability and the account rep is easy to reach. The stationer on Mill Lane put prices up slightly on the survey pads, still cheaper than ordering online with delivery included so staying with them. Looked at a second plant supplier further out for specialist trees the Whitlow project might need, got a quote but nothing ordered yet, keeping it as a backup option. The tool hire place near the industrial estate has been reliable for the bigger kit like the turf cutter, worth remembering for the Oakridge communal areas work coming up later in the year. Also compared a couple of quotes for topsoil delivery since the price seems to have crept up everywhere this year, nothing worth switching over yet but worth keeping an eye on before the bigger Oakridge planting phase starts. Overall suppliers feel more settled than they did at the start of the year, fewer surprises week to week.

Rui had a check up at the doctors, all fine, just the usual growth chart update. Little Acorns nursery is doing a spring open morning for parents, Jordan is planning to go since Sam has a work thing that morning. Rui has started saying full sentences more consistently, nursery staff say it is coming along nicely for the age group. Bought a smaller pair of wellies since the old ones do not fit anymore, useful with the garden being muddy after all the rain this month. Rui has also taken a real shine to one of the other kids at nursery, they seem to play together most days now which is nice to hear about at pickup. Thinking about whether to start Rui on a second activity alongside swimming later in the year, nothing decided, just something Sam and Jordan have been chatting about. The wellies were bought at the shop on Mill Lane on the way back from the studio, easier than ordering online and waiting for delivery. Nothing else to note, a fairly ordinary stretch at home.

The personal mailbox got a bit cluttered with newsletters, spent twenty minutes unsubscribing from a handful that never get read. The work mailbox is fine, mostly client and supplier threads, easy enough to keep on top of daily. Checked the college mailbox after not looking at it for over a week, a couple of student questions were waiting, replied to both. Worth remembering to check the college one more regularly during term time since students sometimes need a same day answer about class times. The notes app synced a bit slowly on the phone this week, seemed to sort itself out after a restart, nothing to chase up about it yet. Also spent a few minutes tidying the task app, marked a handful of old finished jobs as done that had been sitting there for weeks, satisfying to clear the list down a bit even if it does not change anything practically. Worth doing this kind of admin tidy up more often rather than letting it build up for months at a time.

Team catch up notes. Tomasz is thinking about doing a short course on drainage systems next year, would be useful for the bigger public projects like Halden and Oakridge. Priya asked about adjusting her hours slightly for the summer to fit around a family thing, agreed to sort out a schedule once the details are clearer. Discussed whether the studio needs a second van given how much driving happens between three active sites at once, decided to hold off for now and see how the year goes. Everyone seems to be managing the current workload fine even with the college course taking up two evenings a week of Jordan's time. Also talked briefly about whether to take on a placement student for the summer through the college, nothing firm yet, would depend on whether there is enough straightforward work to hand over without slowing the current projects down. Agreed to revisit the idea again once the Halden presentation is out of the way and there is more headspace to think it through properly.

End of summer finance notes. The studio's insurance renewal is coming up in October, Dana already has the paperwork started. Went through outstanding invoices, only one small one still open with a new client from earlier in the year, sent a polite reminder. Costs for plant material have crept up slightly this year across the board, factoring that into quotes for new enquiries going forward rather than absorbing it. Dana also mentioned the studio should think about a pension contribution review before the tax year ends, nothing urgent but worth putting time aside for in the autumn. Also went over the year so far against the original budget Dana put together in January, tracking close enough that nothing needs adjusting, just good to check in on every so often rather than assume it is all fine. Dana will pull together a fuller forecast for the last quarter once the Oakridge planting invoices are in.

Project status round up before the summer. Halden Parks Trust meadow is now in its establishment phase, mostly monitoring and a bit of watering support until autumn. Oakridge Housing Co-op's communal planting beds are next up once the irrigation trenching wraps, aiming to start planting in September. The Whitlow family garden is essentially finished bar the roses that needed replacing, a final walkthrough with the family is booked for next month. No new big projects confirmed yet though there are two enquiries at quote stage that could turn into autumn work if they go ahead. Overall the first half of the year has gone roughly to plan, the public projects took longer to get moving than expected but are both in a good place now heading into the second half. Will circle back on the two open enquiries in a couple of weeks if neither has replied by then, no point chasing too soon and putting anyone off.

Pickle had his annual vet check, all good, just the usual booster done at the same time. He has picked up a habit of digging near the greenhouse which is mildly annoying but easy enough to fence off with some mesh for now. Sam has been taking him on longer evening walks since the weather has been good, seems to have settled him a bit. Rui likes helping fill his water bowl, mostly successfully. The vet mentioned Pickle is carrying a little extra weight for his size, nothing serious, just worth cutting back on treats slightly and keeping the walks consistent rather than only on the good weather days. Booked the next annual check for roughly the same time next year, the surgery only takes phone bookings on Tuesday and Thursday mornings so put a reminder in the task app well ahead of time this time round rather than leaving it to the last minute. Nothing else to report there, an easy stretch with the dog lately.

Dealt with some college admin this week. The end of spring term paperwork needs the attendance register and a short feedback summary from the group, put both together and sent over. The college mentioned a possible pay rate review for evening course tutors starting next academic year, nothing confirmed, just a heads up email from their HR department. Also asked about whether the course could run as two shorter modules instead of one long one, floated the idea to the course coordinator to think about for future terms. Term wrapped up on a good note, several students said they wanted to come back for a follow on course if one gets offered. Handed back the borrowed planting diagrams to Priya once the last class was done, she was glad to have the originals back before starting on the Whitlow drawings properly. Told the college admin office the term overall went well and asked them to keep Jordan in mind for the autumn schedule.

Kept an eye on what other studios in the area are doing. A newer outfit set up recently doing similar residential work, seems mostly social media focused so far, not clear how established they are yet. The bigger contractor Tomasz used to work for is still mostly doing larger commercial jobs, not really overlapping with Fernline's client base. Nothing to change strategy over, just useful to know who else is around when quoting for new work, especially anything public sector like the Halden or Oakridge type projects where there is sometimes a formal tender process. Priya pointed out that a couple of the newer studios seem to be undercutting heavily on price for small residential jobs, worth keeping quotes realistic rather than chasing every enquiry that comes in at the bottom end of the market. Decided the best approach is still to focus on the kind of design led work the studio is known for rather than compete purely on price.

Mid year accounts review with Dana. Overall revenue is tracking slightly ahead of the same point last year, mostly thanks to the Halden and Oakridge contracts landing earlier than expected. Costs are roughly where expected too, plant material and fuel for the van being the two biggest variable costs month to month. Dana raised the idea of moving to a proper payroll system if the studio ever takes on a fourth person, currently everyone is paid simply enough that it has not been necessary. Also confirmed the studio is not close to any VAT threshold issues beyond the standard registration already in place. Dana suggested revisiting the equipment replacement pot again in the autumn once the printer situation becomes clearer, no rush on that for now since the current one is still limping along fine. Overall a positive check in, nothing that needs urgent attention before the next quarterly review.

Spent some time getting familiar with the newer version of the Thornfield ordering portal after their update earlier in the summer. Layout is a bit different, took a few tries to find the saved order templates which used to be on the first screen and are now under a separate tab. Delivery slot booking seems faster than before, used to take a couple of days to confirm and now it is usually same day. Nothing to flag as broken, just a bit of relearning where things live in the new layout, worth mentioning to Tomasz and Priya since they also place orders sometimes. Sent a short note round to the team with a couple of screenshots showing where the templates moved to, should save everyone a few minutes of hunting around the next time they need to place an order. Overall the update seems like an improvement once the initial relearning curve is out of the way, faster delivery slots make the biggest practical difference day to day.
